```{r setup}
#| include: false
# quarto's R may start in a C locale; keep characters such as the degree sign intact
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8"))
library(tidyverse)
library(ramb)
```

The ping chapter (@sec-pings) shows each rule of step 0 on a case or two. This appendix scores them all at once, ping
by ping, on ramb's planted faults. `dansk_planted` is the Danish tracks made clean, thinned to four ping rates (ten
seconds, a minute, six minutes and an hour), with faults planted in each vessel's track at each rate and every ping
labelled with what was done to it. The faults are a position moved (a spike), a run of three to eight moved together,
a position moved aside and back under 25 knots (an out-and-back), a placeholder, the first ping after a gap moved,
copies of reports (a stretch from another day, a second feed whose clock runs late or an hour late in summer, a report
sent again a second later), and a second feed reporting the same second elsewhere (a tie). One fast passage per
vessel, at 30 to 40 knots, is not a fault: a filter should keep it.

Every ping falls in one outcome (`rb_add_ping_outcome()`). A wrong ping is caught, caught as another kind (a copy
flagged as a bad position), or missed. A good ping is kept, or flagged: on its own, or beside a fault. The two are told
apart by running the same rule on the tracks without their wrong pings: a good ping flagged there too is the rule's own
flag. Each rule runs after the placeholders and the copies (`rb_flag_ping_invalid()`, then
`rb_flag_ping_duplicate()` with the recorded speed and course), as ramb advises.

```{r}
#| include: false
planted <- rb_read_example("dansk_planted") |> collect() |>
  arrange(vid, time, .rid) |>
  mutate(stream = feed,   # each feed is a stream of its own here
         truth = case_when(fault %in% c("shifted_copy", "clock_offset", "summer_time", "near_copy") ~ "copy",
                           wrong ~ "flag position",
                           TRUE ~ "keep"))
limits <- rb_create_ping_limits(planted, speed = speed)
copies_out <- function(x, recorded = TRUE) {
  x <- rb_flag_ping_invalid(x)
  if (recorded) {
    rb_flag_ping_duplicate(x, priority = c("a", "b"), feed = feed, speed = speed, course = course)
  } else {
    rb_flag_ping_duplicate(x, priority = c("a", "b"), feed = feed)
  }
}
rules <- list(
  `clean` = function(x) rb_flag_ping_impossible(x, method = "clean", feed = feed),
  `forward` = function(x) rb_flag_ping_impossible(x, method = "forward", feed = feed),
  `local, no recorded speed` = function(x) rb_flag_ping_impossible(x, method = "local", feed = feed),
  `local, recorded speed` = function(x) rb_flag_ping_impossible(x, method = "local", speed = speed, feed = feed),
  `+ own limits` = function(x) {
    rb_flag_ping_impossible(x, method = "local", speed = speed, limits = limits, feed = feed)
  },
  `+ the vote` = function(x) {
    rb_flag_ping_impossible(x, method = "local", speed = speed, limits = limits, anchor = "vote", feed = feed)
  },
  `+ each stream apart` = function(x) {
    rb_flag_ping_impossible(x, method = "local", speed = speed, limits = limits, anchor = "vote", feed = feed,
                            stream = stream)
  })
score <- function(pre, rule) {
  judged <- rule(pre)
  alone <- rule(pre |> filter(truth == "keep")) |> select(.rid, alone_flag = ping_flag)
  judged |> left_join(alone, by = ".rid") |>
    rb_add_ping_outcome(ping_flag, truth, clean = alone_flag, name = "outcome")
}
pre <- copies_out(planted)
scored <- imap_dfr(rules, function(rule, name) score(pre, rule) |> mutate(rule = name))
# every ping in one outcome, under every rule
stopifnot(all(count(scored, rule)$n == nrow(planted)), !anyNA(scored$outcome))
rule_order <- names(rules)
rate_lab <- c(`10` = "10 s", `60` = "1 min", `360` = "6 min", `3600` = "1 h")
by_rate <- scored |>
  group_by(rule = factor(rule, rule_order), rate = factor(rate_lab[as.character(rate_s)], rate_lab)) |>
  summarise(caught = 100 * mean(outcome[truth == "flag position"] %in% c("caught", "caught, as copy", "caught, as time")),
            own = 1e4 * mean(outcome[truth == "keep"] == "flagged"),
            beside = 1e4 * mean(outcome[truth == "keep"] == "flagged, beside a fault"),
            fishing = 1e4 * mean(outcome[truth == "keep" & fishing] != "kept"),
            .groups = "drop")
wide <- function(v, digits = 1) {
  by_rate |> select(rule, rate, value = all_of(v)) |>
    mutate(value = round(value, digits)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = rate, values_from = value)
}
```

## By ping rate

The seven rules run from the fixed ceiling to ramb's advice and one step past it. `"clean"` and `"forward"` judge
every leg at 25 knots. `"local"` without a recorded speed does too, with its own two stages. Given the recorded speed,
it judges each leg at the speed the vessel records around it; each line after adds one setting to the one before:
each vessel's own limits, the vote at a jump, and each feed judged as a stream apart. The line `+ the vote` is ramb's
advice.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-caught
#| tbl-cap: "Wrong positions caught (%), by rule and ping rate: the spikes, runs, out-and-backs, placeholders, first pings after a gap and the wrong reports of a tie."
wide("caught") |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-own
#| tbl-cap: "Good pings flagged on the rule's own, in 10,000 good pings: flagged also on the tracks without their wrong pings. The fast passages count as good pings."
wide("own") |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-beside
#| tbl-cap: "Good pings flagged beside a fault, in 10,000 good pings: flagged only where the wrong pings are there."
wide("beside") |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-fishing
#| tbl-cap: "Good pings flagged while fishing, in 10,000 good fishing pings, the rule's own and beside a fault together: what a rule takes from the effort."
wide("fishing") |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| include: false
at <- function(v, r, rt) by_rate |> filter(rule == r, rate == rt) |> pull(all_of(v))
```

Read together: the recorded speed is the large step. With it, `"local"` catches more at every rate and its own false
flags fall from about `r round(at("own", "clean", "1 min"))` in 10,000 to `r round(at("own", "local, recorded speed", "1 min"), 1)`
at a ping a minute, since a fast vessel is no longer flagged for being fast. The vessels' own limits move the catch
by a few points either way: up from `r round(at("caught", "local, recorded speed", "10 s"))` to
`r round(at("caught", "+ own limits", "10 s"))` % at ten seconds, down from
`r round(at("caught", "local, recorded speed", "1 min"))` to `r round(at("caught", "+ own limits", "1 min"))` % at a
minute, where they let more of the out-and-backs through (@tbl-scores-fault-1min). The vote adds a few points of catch at the sparse rates
(`r round(at("caught", "+ own limits", "6 min"))` to `r round(at("caught", "+ the vote", "6 min"))` % at six minutes)
and flags fewer good pings beside a fault. Judging each stream apart flags fewer still beside a fault, at a cost in
catch at every rate (`r round(at("caught", "+ the vote", "1 min"))` to `r round(at("caught", "+ each stream apart", "1 min"))` %
at a minute): the ties, two reports of one second in two feeds, show only on a leg between the feeds. At six minutes
and an hour `"forward"` takes the fewest good pings in all, and the fewest from the fishing.

## By fault

```{r}
#| include: false
faults <- c(spike = "a position moved", run = "a run of 3-8 moved", detour = "an out-and-back under 25 kn",
            lon_eq_lat = "a placeholder", first_after_gap = "the first ping after a gap",
            tie = "a tie, the wrong report", shifted_copy = "a stretch from another day",
            clock_offset = "a second feed, its clock late", summer_time = "a second feed, an hour late",
            near_copy = "a report sent again", fast = "a fast passage (to keep)")
by_fault <- function(r) {
  scored |> filter(rate_s == r, fault %in% names(faults), !(fault == "tie" & truth == "keep")) |>
    group_by(fault = factor(faults[fault], faults), rule = factor(rule, rule_order)) |>
    summarise(flagged = round(100 * mean(!is.na(ping_flag))), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = flagged)
}
```

Each fault's share flagged by any label, at a ping a minute and at one every six minutes. A second feed's copies and
a report sent again are labelled by the copy rule before any speed rule runs, so they differ little between the
rules. A stretch from another day is only paired by it, and the speed rules catch its pings as positions. The fast
passage is the one row where a lower share is better.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-fault-1min
#| tbl-cap: "Each planted fault flagged (%), by rule, at a ping a minute (`dansk_planted`)."
by_fault(60) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-fault-6min
#| tbl-cap: "Each planted fault flagged (%), by rule, at a ping every six minutes (`dansk_planted`)."
by_fault(360) |> knitr::kable()
```

## The copies first, or not

```{r}
#| include: false
advised <- rules[["+ the vote"]]
copies_compared <- bind_rows(
  score(copies_out(planted, recorded = FALSE), advised) |> mutate(copies = "across feeds, at one time"),
  score(pre, advised) |> mutate(copies = "and one report twice (speed, course)"))
copy_kinds <- copies_compared |> filter(truth == "copy") |>
  mutate(fault = factor(faults[fault], faults)) |>
  count(copies, fault, outcome) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
good_cost <- copies_compared |> filter(truth == "keep") |>
  group_by(copies) |>
  summarise(`good pings flagged` = sum(outcome != "kept"), `of them fishing` = sum(outcome != "kept" & fishing))
```

The copy rule has two parts: a copy across feeds at one time, which needs only the feeds, and one report twice at any
time, which needs the recorded speed and course. With the second part, most of the late second feed's copies are
labelled as copies (`shifted`) rather than left to the speed rule (@tbl-scores-copies), and the speed rule then takes
fewer good pings: `r format(good_cost[["good pings flagged"]][2], big.mark = ",")` over the four rates, against
`r format(good_cost[["good pings flagged"]][1], big.mark = ",")` after the first part alone
(@tbl-scores-copies-cost). A stretch copied from another day in one feed has no witness here, so its pings are
paired and kept; the speed rule catches them as positions either way.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-copies
#| tbl-cap: "The planted copies under ramb's advised speed rule (`\"local\"` with the recorded speed, own limits and the vote), after the copy rule's first part alone or both parts, all four ping rates: each copy's outcome."
copy_kinds |> knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scores-copies-cost
#| tbl-cap: "Good pings flagged by the same rule, after either copy rule, all four ping rates."
good_cost |> knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```
